title: 5 Reasons to Choose Homeschooling in India
author: Vanshika Parmar
body:
Education is the cornerstone of a child’s development, and parents in India are keenly aware of this fact. However, the traditional schooling system may not always be the best fit for every child. As a result, an increasing number of parents in India are turning to homeschooling, a unique approach to education that offers several advantages over traditional schools.

Homeschooling allows parents to take a more active role in their child’s education, providing them with the freedom and flexibility to tailor the curriculum to their child’s needs and interests. This personalized approach can help children to achieve academic excellence while also fostering their creativity and passion for learning.

In this post, we’ll go into more detail about the reasons why parents in India are increasingly choosing to homeschool their children. This post will provide you with important insights and knowledge on the advantages of homeschooling, whether you are thinking about it for your child or are just interested in this alternative method.

### 1. Academic Excellence

Academic excellence is a crucial aspect of education that parents are keen on achieving for their children. Unfortunately, traditional schooling may not always be the best option for academic achievement. The one-size-fits-all approach used in traditional schooling may not cater to each child’s individual learning needs and may lead to academic struggles.

One advantage of homeschooling is that it permits personalized learning, which has a big influence on academic success. Children who are homeschooled can study at their speed and in a fashion that fits their learning preferences. Personalized learning results in a more in-depth knowledge of the content, which leads to improved academic achievement.

Moreover, the individualized attention that homeschooling provides enhances academic achievement. In traditional schools, children may struggle to get individualized attention from their teachers due to large class sizes. However, homeschooling allows for one-on-one instruction, which means that children can receive the undivided attention of their parents, who can adjust the teaching style to suit their child’s learning style. This enhances the child’s understanding of the material, leading to academic success.

Homeschooling also promotes critical thinking skills and independence in children. Children who are homeschooled are encouraged to explore topics on their own and to seek out answers to their questions. This promotes a deeper understanding of the material and helps children to become independent learners. Independent learners tend to perform better academically because they take responsibility for their learning and are more engaged in the learning process.

Overall, homeschooling can contribute significantly to academic excellence. Personalized learning and individualized attention are critical factors that enhance academic achievement in homeschooled children. Moreover, homeschooling promotes critical thinking skills and independence, which are crucial for academic success. Homeschooling provides a solution to the academic struggles that some children may face in traditional schools and offers a personalized approach that caters to each child’s unique needs and interests.

### 2. Flexibility

Flexibility is one of the key benefits of homeschooling, and it offers a stark contrast to the rigid nature of traditional schooling. Traditional schools follow a set schedule, with little room for deviation. This has caused stress and anxiety for some children, who may struggle to keep up with the pace of the curriculum or may not be able to focus during certain times of the day.

Homeschooling, on the other hand, allows for a more flexible schedule and curriculum. Parents who homeschool their children can design a schedule that works best for their family, taking into consideration their child’s needs and interests. This can lead to a more relaxed and enjoyable learning experience, without the pressure of strict schedules and deadlines.

Moreover, homeschooling provides flexibility in terms of the curriculum. Parents can tailor the curriculum to their child’s unique needs and interests, allowing for a more personalized learning experience. Homeschooled children can also focus on topics that they are passionate about, which can lead to a deeper level of engagement and learning.

Flexibility in homeschooling can benefit both the child and the family. For example, a child who is interested in a particular subject can spend more time on that topic, without being held back by the pace of the curriculum. This can lead to a higher level of academic achievement and a greater sense of fulfillment.

Additionally, homeschooling allows for more family time and can provide opportunities for parents to bond with their children. Homeschooled children can also participate in extracurricular activities during the day, which can be difficult to do in a traditional school setting.

In short, homeschooling offers flexibility in both scheduling and curriculum, allowing for a more personalized and enjoyable learning experience. This can lead to a deeper level of engagement and academic achievement. Homeschooling also provides opportunities for family bonding and extracurricular activities, making it a great option for families who value flexibility and individualized learning.

### 3. Learning Challenges

For children with learning challenges, traditional schools can be a tough environment due to their rigid curriculum and structure. This can take a toll on their academic performance and emotional well-being, which can be tough for parents who are struggling to find a suitable learning environment for their children.

The good news is that homeschooling can provide an excellent alternative that caters to the unique needs of these children. With a flexible and customizable approach to learning, homeschooling allows parents to adjust the curriculum and teaching methods to match their child’s strengths and weaknesses. This personalized approach makes it easier for children with learning challenges to understand and retain information.

In addition, homeschooling provides a nurturing and supportive environment where children can feel safe and encouraged to succeed. Traditional schools can be intimidating for these children, causing them to feel left out and inadequate. Homeschooling offers a comforting atmosphere where children can get the support they need to boost their self-esteem and emotional well-being.

Overall, homeschooling is an excellent option that provides a positive and supportive learning environment for children with learning challenges. By offering a personalized approach to learning and a nurturing environment, homeschooling can help these children to thrive both academically and emotionally.

### 5. School Phobia

School phobia, also known as school refusal, can have significant negative effects on a child’s academic and emotional well-being. Children who suffer from this condition experience intense anxiety or fear about attending school, which can be caused by a variety of factors, including separation anxiety, bullying, or academic pressure. The pressure to attend school and the fear of being in an unfamiliar environment can exacerbate their anxiety and cause them to fall behind academically.

The effects of school phobia can be severe and long-lasting, impacting a child’s self-esteem, social development, and overall well-being. Children who suffer from school phobia may experience feelings of isolation, hopelessness, and depression. Moreover, they may develop a negative association with learning and education, which can have significant implications for their future academic and professional success.

Fortunately, homeschooling can provide a solution for children who suffer from school phobia. Homeschooling allows children to learn in a familiar and comfortable environment, reducing their anxiety and helping them to focus on their studies. Moreover, homeschooling provides a more flexible schedule that can be tailored to meet the needs of the child, allowing for breaks or time off when needed.

In addition, homeschooling provides the opportunity for parents to work closely with their children to identify and address the underlying causes of their school phobia. By providing a safe and supportive environment, parents can work with their children to develop coping strategies and techniques to manage their anxiety. This can include counseling, therapy, or other interventions that can help the child to overcome their fears and succeed academically.

Furthermore, homeschooling can provide a more individualized approach to learning that can help children with school phobia to succeed academically. By learning at their own pace and in a way that suits their unique learning style, homeschooled children can better understand and retain information, leading to improved academic performance and increased confidence in their abilities.

In the end, homeschooling can provide a safe and comfortable environment for children with school phobia to learn and thrive. By providing a nurturing and supportive environment, homeschooling can help children with school phobia to develop the skills and confidence they need to succeed both academically and emotionally.

### 5. Safety, Security, and Well-being of Children

As parents, we all want our children to be safe, secure, and happy. However, traditional schooling may not always provide the assurance that we seek for our children’s well-being. With the increasing incidents of bullying, violence, and harassment in schools, parents are understandably concerned about the safety and security of their children in the traditional school setup. This can lead to anxiety and fear in both parents and children, impacting their mental health.

The traditional school setup can create an environment that is not conducive to the well-being of all children. The pressure to conform to social norms and meet academic expectations can cause stress and anxiety, leading to mental health issues. Children who do not fit into the mainstream mold may feel left out and excluded, leading to feelings of isolation and loneliness.

This is where homeschooling comes in as a viable alternative that provides a safe and secure environment for children to learn. Homeschooling allows parents to be in control of their child’s education, providing a personalized learning experience that caters to their child’s needs and interests. This can lead to a sense of purpose and fulfillment in children, contributing to their overall well-being.

Moreover, homeschooling provides an opportunity for parents to monitor their child’s social interactions, reducing the risk of bullying and harassment. By eliminating the stress and anxiety caused by the traditional school setup, homeschooling provides an environment that promotes the mental health and well-being of children.

In short, homeschooling provides a solution to the safety and security concerns that parents face in traditional schooling. By offering a personalized learning experience that caters to the needs and interests of each child, homeschooling promotes the mental health and well-being of children. As parents, it is our responsibility to ensure that our children receive the education and support they need to thrive, and homeschooling provides an alternative that allows us to do just that.

In conclusion, homeschooling in India offers numerous benefits that can help children to thrive both academically and emotionally. Homeschooling provides a more flexible and customized approach to learning that can be tailored to suit the needs and strengths of each individual child. Additionally, homeschooling also provides a safe and supportive environment that can help children to develop the skills and confidence they need to succeed.

For parents who are considering homeschooling as an option for their child’s education, it is important to carefully consider the benefits and challenges of this approach. Homeschooling requires a significant amount of time, effort, and dedication on the part of the parent, but the rewards can be significant.

If you are a parent considering homeschooling for your child, it is important to research your options, seek out support and resources, and consult with other homeschooling families to learn more about the process. With dedication and hard work, homeschooling can be a rewarding and fulfilling experience for both you and your child.

title: Homeschooling- The New Schooling in India
author: Vanshika Parmar
body:
Are you seeking a different approach to school that will provide your child with a more individualized, flexible, and personalised learning experience? Have you given homeschooling a thought? Homeschooling is becoming more and more common in India, and families are using it as an alternative education strategy to provide their children with a special and individualized educational experience.

This blog will cover all the information you need to know about homeschooling in India, including its historical origins, the admissions procedure, and the advantages of this alternative teaching strategy. We’ll also explore why families decide to homeschool their children as well as possible career paths for homeschooled students.

We are here to help you through the process and provide you with important information so you can make an educated decision about your child’s education, whether you are a parent thinking about homeschooling for your child or are just interested in this alternative education option. So let’s dig in and learn more about homeschooling in India!

### What is Homeschooling?

Let’s face it, traditional schooling isn’t for everyone. With the rise of modern education, homeschooling has become an increasingly popular alternative for parents who want to provide their children with a personalized and flexible education. Homeschooling is a parent-directed education method that involves teaching your child from home instead of sending them to a traditional classroom setting. It’s a great way to give your child a tailored education that fits their individual needs and interests.

The freedom that homeschooling provides is one of its major benefits. Parents have the autonomy to choose their own curriculum, create a schedule that works for their family’s lifestyle, and even take their child’s education on the road. This is especially appealing to families who travel often or have a child with a passion for the arts or athletics that requires more flexibility in their schedule.

But the benefits of homeschooling don’t stop there. Homeschooled students often receive personalized instruction and one-on-one attention, which can lead to better academic performance. In fact, many homeschooled students have achieved incredible success in various fields. The winner of the 2020 Scripps National Spelling Bee was a homeschooled student, and homeschooled actors and musicians such as Jennifer Love Hewitt and Taylor Swift have become household names.

It’s important to understand the distinction between homeschooling and unschooling. While homeschooling follows a structured curriculum, unschooling is a more radical approach to education that encourages children to learn from life experiences rather than a prescribed curriculum. In India, unschooling may not be recognized as a valid form of education, which is why many families choose homeschooling instead.

### Growth of Homeschooling in India

Homeschooling has been gaining popularity in India in recent years, with more and more families opting for this alternative method of education. Homeschooling in India has its roots in ancient times when children were taught by their parents or gurus in a one-on-one setting. However, the modern homeschooling movement began in the late 1980s and early 1990s when parents started questioning the traditional education system’s effectiveness.

The growing popularity of homeschooling is mostly due to worries about the standard of teaching in regular institutions. A lot of parents believe that the standard school curriculum is obsolete and unprepared for the world that is changing so quickly. Children can learn at their own speed and concentrate on subjects that interest them when they are homeschooled, which offers a more individualized approach to education.

Another reason for the increase in the popularity of homeschooling is the availability of Edtech innovations. With the advent of online learning platforms, parents can now access high-quality educational resources and curricula without having to rely on traditional schools. These resources can be tailored to the individual needs of the child, making learning more effective and engaging.

The COVID-19 pandemic has also played a significant role in the growth of homeschooling in India. The pandemic forced schools to close, and many parents turned to homeschooling as an alternative to ensure their children’s education did not suffer. This shift has opened up new opportunities for homeschooling and demonstrated the effectiveness of this method of education.

There is evidence of the steady growth of homeschooling in India, with an increasing number of families opting for this alternative method of education. Homeschooled students are also gaining recognition from college admissions boards, who appreciate the unique skills and experiences they bring to the table. For instance, many homeschooled students have demonstrated exceptional creativity, critical thinking skills, and a passion for learning.

overall, homeschooling in India has a rich history and is becoming an increasingly popular alternative to traditional schooling. This growth can be attributed to concerns about the quality of education in traditional schools, the availability of Edtech innovations, and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. As more families turn to homeschooling, it is clear that this method of education has the potential to create well-rounded, independent learners who are prepared for the challenges of the future.

### Benefits of Homeschooling

Let’s explore some of the amazing advantages of homeschooling.

#### 1. Personalized education for children

Traditional schools sometimes follow a one-size-fits-all philosophy of education, yet each child is different and has their own strengths and limitations. When a child is homeschooled, parents can modify their education to fit their child’s requirements and learning preferences. For instance, you may use more visual aids in your child’s lessons if they are visual learners to assist them to comprehend the subject matter.

#### 2. Attention to Concepts and Details

Because homeschooling involves one-on-one instruction, children are able to receive more attention and feedback from their parents or tutors. This can help them develop a stronger foundation in their studies and master concepts that may be more difficult in a traditional classroom setting.

#### 3. flexibility and freedom for children

Children who are homeschooled are allowed to explore their hobbies and interests in ways that regular institutions might not be able to. If your child is interested in art, for instance, they can spend additional time on projects and attend lessons or workshops outside of the regular school day.

#### 4. focusing on their strengths and limitations

When children are homeschooled, parents and tutors have the opportunity to really get to know their children and understand their learning styles. This can help them create a more effective curriculum and tailor their teaching methods to their child’s strengths and weaknesses.

#### 5. Formalization of homeschooling

Homeschooling is increasingly being formalized and acknowledged as a legitimate educational option in several nations, including India, to guarantee that it is equivalent to other educational options. As a result, students who are homeschooled are eligible to sit for tests and earn diplomas that are comparable to those from regular schools. This is excellent news for parents who wish to provide their children with a high-quality education while also allowing for the freedom and personalization that come with homeschooling.

Overall, homeschooling offers a unique and flexible approach to education that can benefit children in many ways. With customization, personalized attention, and the freedom to explore passions, homeschooled students can thrive academically and personally. And with the growing recognition of homeschooling as a legitimate form of education, the possibilities for success are endless.

### Main Boards for Homeschooling in India

Since homeschooling has gained such broad acceptance in India, open education and learning have been formalized further to make sure that those who participate in it don’t fall short in any manner. Major academic institutions, both domestically and internationally, have started to use this alternate kind of education. The two main associations concerning homeschooling in India are listed below:

#### National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS)

An open learning organization called the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) in India gives students the tools they need to complete their education while attending home school. According to this board, parents are permitted to homeschool their kids and have them take important tests like the class 10th and 12th grades. Students must register with the board, and the certification obtained through the tests offered by it is equivalent to that obtained from any other board in the country. It provides education at various levels and places an emphasis on vocational training in addition to formal education.

#### International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE)

Cambridge’s International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) is an internationally recognized qualification for homeschooling students. It is held in the tenth grade and consists of several phases that assess a child’s learning from the preparatory to the advanced levels. Candidates take the test as private candidates and potentially acquire a globally recognized certification.

### Admission Process for Homeschooling

If you’re considering homeschooling as an alternative to traditional education, you may be wondering about the admission process. The good news is that it’s relatively straightforward

#### Step 1: Research and Decide

The first step is to do your research and decide if homeschooling is the right fit for your child and your family. Consider factors such as your child’s learning style, your availability as a parent or tutor, and your family’s values and goals.

#### Step 2: Find an Open Learning Board

After deciding to homeschool your children, you must locate an open learning community that has obtained official approval. The International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) and the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) are only two of the alternatives offered in India.

#### Step 3: Register with the Open Learning Board

Next, you will need to register your child with the chosen open learning board. This process usually involves submitting an application form along with supporting documents such as a birth certificate, address proof, and previous academic records (if any). The open learning board will provide a registration number and a study material package for your child.

#### Step 4: Create a Curriculum

With the open learning board’s study material as a guide, you can customize a curriculum that fits your child’s interests and learning needs. This is where homeschooling truly shines as it allows for a tailored approach to education.

#### Step 5: Record Keeping

As a homeschooling parent or tutor, you will need to maintain a record of your child’s progress and academic achievements. This will include maintaining a portfolio of your child’s work and grades.

#### Step 6: Annual Assessment

To ensure equivalence to other forms of education, your child will need to undergo an annual assessment by the open learning board. This assessment will test your child’s knowledge and understanding of the subjects they’ve studied during the academic year.

Overall, the admission process for homeschooling in India is fairly straightforward. It involves finding an open learning board, registering your child, creating a customized curriculum, keeping track of progress, and undergoing an annual assessment. With the right resources and support, homeschooling can provide a unique and rewarding educational experience for your child.

### What about your child’s career after homeschooling?

As a homeschooling parent, your primary focus is on providing your child with the best education possible. You spend countless hours researching curriculum options, creating lesson plans, and ensuring that your child receives a well-rounded education. However, as your child approaches the end of high school, you may begin to wonder about their future beyond homeschooling.

you wear many hats as a homeschooling parent, including that of a guidance counselor. While traditionally, high school students rely on guidance counselors to help them make decisions about their future, you have the unique opportunity to play this role for your child. However, we understand that taking on this responsibility can be overwhelming. That’s why we’re here to provide support and guidance at every step of the way.

At Svastrino, we are here to help you guide your child toward a successful future. Our team of experts can work with you and your child to explore their interests, passions, and talents, providing valuable insights into their vocational options after graduation. We believe that a personalized approach is essential to ensure that every child finds their true calling.

Our goal is to arm children with the information and abilities they need to pursue their ideal career path and make wise decisions.

If you’re a homeschooling parent with inquiries regarding what will happen to your child after graduation, get in touch with us. We are here to provide guidance and inspiration at every level, ensuring that your child is well-equipped to achieve their goals and dreams
